title: Thousands Rally Across Turkey After Court Removes CHP Leadership; International Backlash
detail: Thousands of protesters gathered in Istanbul, Ankara, İzmir, and other major Turkish cities on May 22, 2026, in response to the Ankara court's ruling annulling the CHP leadership. CHP offices across the country saw demonstrations, with protesters denouncing the ruling as an attack on democracy. The BIST-100 stock index had already fallen more than 6% on May 21 as investors reacted to increased political uncertainty. Human Rights Watch published a formal condemnation titled 'Türkiye: Court Removes Leadership of Main Opposition Party,' calling it part of a systematic pattern of using courts to suppress political opposition. The European Union issued a statement calling for Turkey to allow the opposition to operate freely, while the US State Department expressed concern about the erosion of democratic norms. The Council of Europe's Venice Commission announced it would review the ruling's compatibility with European democratic standards. CHP announced plans to appeal the ruling at Turkey's constitutional court while calling emergency sessions of its parliamentary group.

media.caption: Thousands protest across Turkey after court removes CHP leadership — May 22, 2026

title: Rubio–Fidan Bilateral at NATO Helsingborg FM Meeting; Ankara Summit Agenda Set
detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met bilaterally on the sidelines of the NATO Foreign Ministers Meeting in Helsingborg, Sweden (May 21–22, 2026), the last major ministerial gathering before the July 7–8 NATO Summit in Ankara. According to the US State Department readout, discussions covered preparation for the Ankara summit, defense spending commitments, Strait of Hormuz access, and regional stability — particularly regarding the Middle East and Syria's post-Assad transition. The meeting signals a cautious warming in US–Turkey relations ahead of Turkey's first hosting of a NATO summit. Fidan separately stated the Ankara summit should 'reaffirm the alliance's unity and integrity' as European NATO allies face sustained US pressure to increase defense expenditures toward and beyond 2% of GDP.

media.caption: Secretary Rubio meets FM Fidan at NATO Helsingborg ministerial — May 22, 2026
